mostWorthwhile.text: Using the spindle on the copied DNA was most worthwhile: the planned time strip connects chromosome separation to two complete daughter nuclei while showing that the cytoplasm is still joined.

leastWorthwhile.text: Preparing and then adding membrane were clear but relatively predictable, since each goal named the needed materials or action.

surprise.text: The spindle appeared first as a preview of assembly during mitosis, rather than as a structure already attached to chromosomes; the timing caption helped clarify that distinction.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the broad title “New cell proteins” did not itself explain which proteins form spindle fibres; the result identifies tubulin.

continue.text: I would continue: the chapter’s linked constructions made genome copying and division understandable, and the later differentiation paths suggest a useful next question. The highly explicit goals did make the choices straightforward.
